summary: Four end-to-end integration scenarios — happy path, mid-day API outage, container restart with crash-loop guard, manual-review preemption. Tests are integration-pyramid appropriate (4 tests, ~644 LoC), use real SQLite via tempfile, mock only the genuine boundary (Claude/Google/Telegraph/Telegram). Truth source for slot timing is compute_publish_slots itself, not hard-coded values — meets task constraint. All 4 pass.

findings.title: Scenario 1 admin-ping assertion is loose (any-of two fragments)
findings.description: Assertion 'any("расписание" in m or "Зафетчил" in m for m in msgs)' permits two distinct ping shapes. Spec asks 'plan of day fragment', which is the schedule announcement. If both pings exist concurrently, this still passes — fine. But a future change that drops both still goes undetected if the catch-phrase changes. Acceptable per task hint 'check by fragment/semantics, not exact match'.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable. Aligns with spec hint about loose admin-ping assertions to allow future stylistic edits.

findings.title: Scenario 2 does not assert ping #1 vs ping #2 differentiation
findings.description: Test asserts SOMETHING containing 'Claude API недоступна' was sent. With a single ClaudeOutageError raised on slot 2, the state machine should advance from 0 → 1, sending only ping #1. If a regression causes ping #1 AND ping #2 to fire on the same event, this assertion still passes. Could tighten by asserting exactly one such ping.
findings.recommendation: Optional. ping_count assertion at line 417 already pins state to 1, which indirectly bounds ping count. Acceptable.

findings.title: Scenario 3 doesn't verify slot timing matches compute_publish_slots output for the 5-pending case
findings.description: The test verifies the FIRST sleep is the crash-loop guard wait. It does not verify the 5 subsequent slot waits match compute_publish_slots(5, 16:00 MSK). Spec says 'sverify with compute_publish_slots contract for same inputs, not hard-coded'. Adding such an assertion would tighten coverage of AC3-AC6 in the restart path.
findings.recommendation: Could add. Scenario 1 already covers the slot-timing-matches-compute_publish_slots assertion explicitly. Scenario 3's primary purpose is the recompute and crash-loop guard, both of which ARE asserted. Acceptable as-is.

findings.title: Scenario 4 doesn't assert no admin error-ping fired
findings.description: Test asserts no duplicate, no error in published rows. It does NOT explicitly assert that no error-shaped admin notification was sent during the loop (e.g., 'failed to publish'). If a regression caused the bot to log+notify an error when it found a row missing, the test would still pass. Could add: assertFalse(any('error' in m.lower() for m in self._admin_messages())).
findings.recommendation: Minor improvement. Could add for robustness.

findings.title: Scenario 4 docstring describes the timing of the side_effect inaccurately
findings.description: Docstring at 552-556 starts by describing one approach ('side-effect on the second Claude mock call') then redirects to another approach ('callback on the FIRST call'). Reads as a thinking-aloud. Cleaner to describe only the chosen mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Optional cleanup of docstring. Functional behaviour is correct.

findings.title: AC17 marked as 'covered implicitly' but no direct assertion exercises it
findings.description: The module docstring claims AC17 (bot keeps fallback_active until next 12:00 cron tick) is 'covered implicitly'. The is_fallback_active() == False assertion at line 422 is correct for ping #1 (the flag flips only at ping #3). Acceptable but only partial; full AC17 coverage would require simulating ping #3 across multiple cron ticks, which is out of this file's scope.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable. The implicit coverage is documented and accurate for what is testable in a single job() tick.

findings.title: No assertion that send_telegraph_teaser was called for each successful publish
findings.description: The mock_teaser is set up but tests do not assert call_count matches the number of slots. A regression that breaks the teaser dispatch but still moves to published would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Could add a teaser-call-count assertion to scenario 1. Low priority — mock_teaser returning True ensures the teaser code path runs without raising.

findings.title: Test class lacks a docstring-level 'no real network' assertion
findings.description: Spec AC says 'Никаких реальных сетевых вызовов: requests, anthropic.Anthropic, Telegraph, Bot.send_message не должны фактически вызываться (assert через mocks)'. This is satisfied by the mock stack — none of those names are imported, and all bound names through which they would be reached are patched. No explicit assert-not-called test. Acceptable: side-effect of the mock stack is that real calls would error on assertion mismatch, which all 4 tests do.
